content:
As more and more AI agents request "Full Disk Access" on your Mac, Apple says it will make changes to macOS to protect user privacy.

Although the company did not reveal specific details, Apple says users should understand what granting this kind of "extraordinary" access to an app really means.

In a blog post on its Developer site, Apple explained that Full Disk Access in macOS was originally designed "to allow backup apps to function properly on Mac." However, Apple noted that "some developers" are using macOS's Full Disk Access setting in ways "that could put users at risk."

In response, Apple says it will "introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely want to grant this extraordinary level of access to an app must go through very clear steps before they can do so."

The company did not share further details about these controls or its planned changes. However, it said the rise of "increasingly capable, autonomous" AI agents calls for greater attention to privacy and security:

Apple's announcement today comes as tools like Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots grow in popularity. These AI agents run continuously and demand access to large amounts of your personal data, and with Meta Muse in particular, we have already seen some alarming examples.
